selection_notes: Lowest-cost true 500mA-class 3.3V LDO with deep stock. Runner-ups: AP2112K-3.3TRG1 (C51118, $0.16, 600mA), XC6206P332MR ($0.017 but only 200-250mA, misses the tier).
JLC Basic jellybean with 2.1M stock; Basic avoids the extended-part setup fee at assembly. Cheaper Extended clone: AMS1117-3.3 C347222 ($0.043). Allow >=1.3V dropout headroom.
Diodes Inc 5A-rated LDO, best price with healthy stock in the 3A+ class. Runner-up LM1084S-3.3/TR (C259972, $0.37). Genuine LM1085ISX-3.3 is $2.01. Linear at 3A dissipates hard: budget copper area.
Canonical cheap booster. MT3608L (C2932326, $0.044) is cheaper but a 16V-max-input variant. TPS61023 (C919459, $0.27) when synchronous rectification or low-battery behavior matters.

Only big-switch parts genuinely deliver 2A+ at 5V from 3.0-4.2V in. FP6293 (C83576, $0.53, 3.5A switch) covers ~1.5A budget builds. TPS61021A has 71K stock but tops out at 4.4V output, so it is ineligible.
TI 2A synchronous buck at $0.07 with 189K stock. SY8089A1AAC (C479074, $0.09, 282K stock) is equivalent. ME3116 (C97643, $0.14) when Vin can reach 40V.
Fixed-output wide-Vin buck with minimal externals; the standard pick for 12V/24V inputs down to 3.3V.
Same family as AP63203 (one footprint serves both rails).
Best price/stock 3A buck by a wide margin (152K stock). MP1584EN is $2.91 at LCSC despite its cheap-module reputation. XL4015E1 (C51661, $0.67) when 5A or a dirt-simple 180kHz design is acceptable.
469K stock at $0.07. Original TopPower TP4056-42-ESOP8 is C16581 ($0.19). TP4057 (C725791, $0.039, SOT-23-6, 500mA) for tiny boards; MCP73831 (C424093, $0.81) when a name brand is required.

Everlight, responds across visible and IR. PD15-22B/TR8 (C161211, $0.10) is the IR-only twin. VBPW34S (C145262, $0.59) for large-area needs. PT17-21C ($0.06, 0805) is a phototransistor when gain beats linearity.
Cheaper than the 12-bit ADS1015IDGSR ($1.62) in the same snapshot, so the 16-bit part wins on both price and resolution.

Diodes Inc linear hall, well documented and stocked. OH49E (C49021369, $0.28) is a cheaper clone; SS49E (C85697) is the TO-92S through-hole classic. For a digital switch instead, use an omnipolar SOT-23 part like SLSS49E-3 (C2904393, $0.15).
VL53L0X module-on-chip; the hobby standard. VL53L1CXV0FY/1 (C190004, $4.82) doubles the range to 4m.
Cheapest current-production 3-axis part. Stock was moderate (1.3K) at snapshot; LIS3DHTR (C15134, $1.09, 6.2K stock) is the better-stocked fallback. ADXL345 runs $3.45+.
Standalone gyros are effectively EOL at LCSC (L3GD20 unstocked, A3G4250D stock 18 at snapshot), so this row deliberately points at the 6-axis IMU default.
82K stock at $1.54. QMI8658A (C3021082, $1.62, 54K stock) is a close second. MPU-6050 is EOL and now $14.92 at LCSC; avoid in new designs.
Integrated digital pyro sensor (through-hole). AM312 had no stock at snapshot. BISS0001 (C404323, $0.11) is the analog-controller route when paired with a bare pyro element.
Best price/stock by 2x (55K stock at $0.97). TMC2209-LA-T (C2150710, $2.70) for silent StealthChop and UART config; DRV8825PWPR (C81582, $2.17) for supplies up to 45V.
JLC Basic across common values. Representative 10k 0402WGF1002TCE = C25744 ($0.0013, 7.2M stock at snapshot). Specific values resolve within the series.
JLC Basic across common values. Representative 10k 0603WAF1002T5E = C25804 ($0.0033, 7.6M stock at snapshot).
